messages.speaker: Maya Chen
messages.text: The security settings page is getting weird. SSO is under Account, audit exports are under Billing, and API tokens are buried in Developer Tools. This is bad for the enterprise demo.

messages.speaker: Sarah Kim
messages.text: Yeah, the demo issue is real. Buyers keep asking why SSO and audit exports are in different places.

messages.speaker: Priya Shah
messages.text: One option is a Security Center parent section. Move SSO and audit exports there first, then API tokens and SCIM. No permissions redesign, just navigation plus moving existing pages.

messages.speaker: Leo Park
messages.text: That is more work, but it matches where enterprise admin is going. Keeping SSO under Account saves maybe 2 days and creates another cleanup project.

messages.speaker: Maya Chen
messages.text: My only worry is slipping the security review demo. We promised the updated admin flow to design partners before 2026-09-10.

messages.speaker: Priya Shah
messages.text: If we keep the first pass boring, I can have the Security Center section wired by next Thursday. No custom permission scopes in this pass.

messages.speaker: Sarah Kim
messages.text: That would solve the demo issue. Boring is honestly fine here.

messages.speaker: Owen Diaz
messages.text: Works for me. Priya, can you take the nav work? I can move API tokens once the route exists.

messages.speaker: Priya Shah
messages.text: Yep. I'll make Security Center the parent section, move SSO and audit exports first, then SCIM. API tokens can follow after Owen's piece.

messages.speaker: Leo Park
messages.text: Agree. Tradeoff is we accept a basic security IA now instead of doing the full permissions model. Safer than hiding SSO under Account.

messages.speaker: Maya Chen
messages.text: Ok then let's keep permissions redesign out of scope. I want something design partners can use before the Sep 10 demo, not a whole admin rebuild.
